set_title: Headache and bitemporal field loss: which mass in or above the sella
stem: An 8-year-old boy has had headaches for 6 months, and his height has fallen from the 50th to the 5th percentile over 1 year. Visual field testing shows bitemporal hemianopia. MRI shows a calcified cystic mass above the sella.
oneliner: 8M + headaches for 6 months + height drop from 50th to 5th percentile + bitemporal hemianopia + calcified cystic suprasellar mass → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Prolactinoma is a solid sellar tumor with hypogonadism; he is **8**, his mass is **calcified and cystic** and his problem is **growth failure**
whyNot.C: A nonfunctioning macroadenoma is a solid sellar mass in adults; he is **8** with a **calcified cystic** mass above the sella
whyNot.D: Apoplexy is a sudden bleed into a known adenoma; his headaches have lasted **6 months** and the mass is **calcified**
whyNot.E: Excess growth hormone in a child would cause tall stature; his height is **falling**

set_title: Confused or drowsy patient who drinks or has cirrhosis: the liver, thiamine, withdrawal or the kidneys
stem: A 55-year-old man with a 20-year history of heavy alcohol use is brought to the emergency department because of 2 days of drowsiness and confusion. He has ascites and spider angiomata, and he has been constipated for a week. He has nystagmus, weak lateral gaze and a wide-based gait, and no flapping tremor of the outstretched arms. Fingerstick glucose is 96 mg/dL.
oneliner: 55M + heavy alcohol use + drowsy and confused for 2 days + ascites + spider angiomata + nystagmus and wide-based gait, no flapping tremor + glucose 96 → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.C: Hepatic encephalopathy flaps the outstretched arms; his arms show **no flapping tremor** and he has **nystagmus and an ataxic gait**
whyNot.A: Delirium tremens brings agitation, hallucinations and autonomic overactivity; he is **drowsy** with **nystagmus and gait ataxia**
whyNot.D: Uremia causes asterixis and needs kidney failure; he has **no flapping tremor** and his findings are **ocular and cerebellar**
whyNot.E: Hypoglycemia needs a low glucose; his glucose is **96 mg/dL**

why: Thiamine is a cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase and transketolase, so deficiency in a heavy drinker injures the mammillary bodies, thalamus and periaqueductal region. **Confusion with nystagmus, weak lateral gaze and a wide-based gait** is Wernicke encephalopathy, and thiamine is given before glucose.

set_title: Shaking, jerking or slowed movements: basal ganglia, cerebellum or copper
stem: A 66-year-old man has had 2 years of a tremor in his right hand. The tremor is present when his hand rests in his lap and fades when he reaches for a cup. Strength, sensation, reflexes and finger-to-nose testing are normal.
oneliner: 66M + 2 years of right-hand tremor at rest that fades on reaching + normal strength, reflexes and finger-to-nose → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Essential tremor is a postural and action tremor that is absent at rest; his tremor is **present at rest and fades when he reaches**
whyNot.B: Wilson disease starts in the teens to 30s; he is **66 with a tremor that is present at rest**
whyNot.D: Huntington disease causes brief, irregular, jerky movements; his only symptom is a **rest tremor that fades with reaching**
whyNot.E: A cerebellar lesion gives an intention tremor with dysmetria; his **finger-to-nose testing is normal and the tremor fades with reaching**

stem: A 69-year-old man who has diabetes and hypertension has the sudden onset of continuous, wild flinging movements of his left arm and leg. He is alert, and his strength and sensation are normal.
oneliner: 69M + diabetes and hypertension + sudden wild flinging movements of left arm and leg + normal strength → ?

stem: A 48-year-old woman has had 8 months of weakness and wasting of both hands. Fasciculations are visible in her forearms. Her knee and ankle reflexes are brisk and both plantar responses are extensor. Pinprick, temperature, vibration and position sensation are normal.
oneliner: 48F + 8 months of wasted weak hands + fasciculations + brisk reflexes and Babinski signs + normal sensation → ?

whyNot.A: Subacute combined degeneration impairs vibration and position sense; hers is **normal, with wasted hands and fasciculations**
whyNot.C: Brown-Sequard syndrome follows a hemisection with crossed sensory loss; she has **bilateral hand weakness over 8 months and normal sensation**

whyNot.E: An anterior spinal artery infarct is sudden and takes pain and temperature below a level; her illness developed over **8 months with normal sensation**

stem: A 58-year-old man has burning feet at night. He has had type 2 diabetes mellitus for 15 years with a hemoglobin A1c of 10.1%. He drinks no alcohol. Pinprick and vibration sense are reduced in a stocking distribution and his ankle jerks are absent.
oneliner: 58M + burning feet at night + 15 years of diabetes, HbA1c 10.1% + no alcohol + stocking loss of pinprick and vibration + absent ankle jerks → ?

whyNot.A: Alcoholic neuropathy follows heavy drinking; he **drinks no alcohol** and has **15 years of diabetes with an HbA1c of 10.1%**
whyNot.C: Small fiber neuropathy spares vibration sense and ankle jerks; he has **reduced vibration sense and absent ankle jerks**

stem: A 14-year-old boy is struck on the side of the head by a baseball and loses consciousness for a minute. He then talks normally for 2 hours before becoming drowsy. His right pupil is now dilated. CT of the head shows a lens-shaped collection of blood that stops at the suture lines.
oneliner: 14M + baseball blow to the temple, brief unconsciousness, 2-hour lucid interval, then drowsiness and a dilated pupil + lens-shaped collection that stops at the sutures → ?
ask: What is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: An intracerebral hemorrhage is blood inside brain tissue after hypertension; his collection is **lens-shaped, outside the brain, after a head blow with a lucid interval**
whyNot.B: A subarachnoid hemorrhage gives a sudden headache with blood in the cisterns; he had **a blow, a lucid interval and a lens-shaped collection**

The dilated pupil is uncal herniation compressing the oculomotor nerve.

oneliner: 30M + double vision since a head injury 1 week ago + normal lids and pupils: trochlear or abducens palsy? → ?
ask: Which additional finding best favors a trochlear nerve palsy over an abducens nerve palsy?

options.D: Double images that resolve with one eye covered
options.E: Eye movement that is normal on upward gaze

whyNot.B: Lid position is normal in both palsies; it **does not separate them**
whyNot.C: Pupils are normal in both palsies; it **does not separate them**
whyNot.D: Binocular double vision resolves when one eye is covered in either palsy; it **does not separate them**

why: The superior oblique, supplied by the trochlear nerve, depresses and intorts the adducted eye, so its loss causes vertical double vision that is worst on looking down and in, as when reading or going down stairs. stem: A 3-year-old boy who has received no vaccines has had 1 day of fever, vomiting, and a stiff neck. Cerebrospinal fluid shows many neutrophils, a low glucose concentration, and gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci.
oneliner: 3M + no vaccines, 1 day of fever, vomiting, stiff neck + CSF with neutrophils, low glucose, gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci → ?

stem: A 65-year-old man develops sudden vertigo and vomiting. He has hoarseness and difficulty swallowing. Strength is normal, but pain and temperature sensation are lost over the right side of the face and the left arm and leg.
oneliner: 65M + sudden vertigo, hoarseness, dysphagia + crossed pain-temperature loss + normal strength → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Medial medullary syndrome causes opposite-side weakness and loss of vibration with a deviated tongue; his **strength is normal and pain and temperature are lost**
whyNot.B: Weber syndrome causes an oculomotor palsy with opposite-side weakness; he has **vertigo, hoarseness and normal strength**
whyNot.D: Lateral pontine syndrome adds facial paralysis and hearing loss; his bulbar signs are **hoarseness and difficulty swallowing**, which point to the nucleus ambiguus in the medulla

oneliner: 70F + sudden right arm and leg weakness, face spared + right vibration and position loss + tongue deviates left → ?

oneliner: 35F + headaches and right arm clumsiness + cerebellar cyst with enhancing nodule + retinal capillary tumor + renal mass → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Neurofibromatosis type 2 gives bilateral vestibular schwannomas and meningiomas; she has **a cerebellar nodule, a retinal capillary tumor and a kidney mass**
whyNot.C: Sturge-Weber syndrome gives a facial stain with seizures in childhood; she is **an adult with a cerebellar nodule and a kidney mass**
whyNot.D: Tuberous sclerosis gives seizures, skin patches and renal angiomyolipomas; she has **a cerebellar nodule with a retinal capillary tumor**
whyNot.E: Neurofibromatosis type 1 gives cafe-au-lait spots and neurofibromas; she has **a cerebellar nodule with a retinal capillary tumor**

why: Loss of the VHL tumor suppressor on chromosome 3p lets HIF accumulate and drives vascular tumors. **Cerebellar and retinal hemangioblastomas with a renal mass**, usually clear cell carcinoma, is von Hippel-Lindau disease.

stem: A 68-year-old right-handed man is evaluated after a left-hemisphere ischemic stroke. His speech is halting and effortful, in phrases of two or three words, and he follows complex spoken commands correctly. He cannot repeat a sentence the examiner says. His right lower face and right arm are weak.
oneliner: 68M right-handed + stroke + halting 2-3 word speech + follows complex commands + cannot repeat + right face and arm weak → ?

stem: A 27-year-old woman at 20 weeks' gestation has a uterus larger than expected for dates. Ultrasonography shows excess amniotic fluid and a fetus with no skull vault above the orbits. Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein is markedly elevated.
oneliner: 27F at 20 weeks + polyhydramnios + no skull vault above the orbits + very high maternal AFP → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Chiari II malformation has a normal skull with the hindbrain pushed through the foramen magnum; this fetus has **no skull vault**
whyNot.C: Spina bifida occulta has normal alpha-fetoprotein and a lumbar defect; here alpha-fetoprotein is **markedly elevated** and the **skull vault is missing**
whyNot.D: Myelomeningocele is a sac over the spine; this fetus has **no skull vault above the orbits**

why: Failure of the anterior neuropore to close leaves no forebrain or skull vault. The fetus cannot swallow amniotic fluid, so **polyhydramnios with a very high alpha-fetoprotein and no skull vault** is anencephaly.

ask: Which single finding favours Chiari II malformation over Dandy-Walker malformation?

options.A: Hydrocephalus with a rapidly enlarging head circumference
options.B: Presentation during the first weeks after birth
options.C: Vermis and tonsils displaced below the foramen magnum
options.D: Need for ventricular shunting in a large proportion of affected infants

whyNot.E: The stem already says the **hindbrain is abnormal**, which is true of both

set_title: Abnormal movements after an antipsychotic: which reaction and when
stem: A 71-year-old woman who takes no regular medicines has had a tremor of the left hand at rest for 2 years. It has now spread to the left leg, and she moves slowly with increased muscle tone.
oneliner: 71F + no regular medicines + 2 years of left-hand resting tremor spreading to the left leg + slow movement, rigidity → ?
ask: What is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Tardive dyskinesia follows years of an antipsychotic with writhing orofacial movements; she takes **no regular medicines** and has a **resting tremor**
whyNot.C: Drug-induced parkinsonism is symmetric and follows a dopamine blocker; she takes **no regular medicines** and her tremor began **on one side**
whyNot.D: Acute dystonia is a sudden spasm after a dopamine blocker; she takes **no regular medicines** and her course is **2 years**
whyNot.E: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome follows a dopamine blocker with fever; she takes **no regular medicines** and her illness has lasted **2 years**

why: Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta leaves the basal ganglia without dopamine. **A one-sided resting tremor that spreads, with slowness and rigidity, in a patient on no dopamine blocker** is Parkinson disease. Levodopa with carbidopa is the usual treatment.

set_title: Confused, forgetful or out of touch: delirium, dementia, psychosis or dissociation
stem: An 84-year-old woman is seen by the physician with her daughter for confusion. Her blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg and her pulse is 78/min. Her daughter says that over 3 years she has become forgetful, repeats questions, and does not know the date, but she stays alert and attentive.
oneliner: 84F + 3 years of forgetfulness, repeats questions, disoriented to date + alert and attentive → ?
ask: What is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Schizophrenia begins in early adulthood with delusions or hallucinations; she is **84 with 3 years of forgetfulness**
whyNot.C: Dissociative amnesia is a loss of personal memories after trauma; she **repeats questions and has declined slowly over 3 years**
whyNot.D: Frontotemporal dementia starts with personality or language change and spares memory early; she has **forgetfulness and repeated questions**
whyNot.E: Delirium is acute with poor attention; her decline took **3 years and she stays alert and attentive**

set_title: Smoker with a lung mass and something else wrong: which paraneoplastic or local effect
stem: A 72-year-old man who has smoked for 50 years has had 2 months of weakness when rising from a chair and climbing stairs. The weakness eases after he repeats the effort. He has a dry mouth, and knee reflexes are diminished.
oneliner: 72M + 50 years of smoking + proximal weakness for 2 months + eases with repeated effort + dry mouth + diminished knee reflexes → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: SIADH causes hyponatremia with confusion; he has **proximal weakness that eases with repeated effort**
whyNot.B: Superior vena cava syndrome causes facial and arm swelling; he has **proximal weakness with a dry mouth**
whyNot.C: Hypercalcemia from PTHrP causes constipation and confusion; he has **weakness that eases with repeated effort**
whyNot.E: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy causes painful wrists and ankles with clubbing; he has **proximal weakness that eases with effort**

why: Antibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels cut acetylcholine release. Repeated activation builds up calcium, so **strength improves with effort**, unlike myasthenia gravis. Dry mouth and depressed reflexes complete it. It is a paraneoplastic effect, most often of small cell carcinoma.

set_title: Sleepy by day after bad nights: which sleep-breathing or sleep disorder
stem: A 21-year-old woman falls asleep several times a day, including during conversations. Her knees buckle and she falls when she laughs. She sees vivid images just as she falls asleep.
oneliner: 21F + sleep attacks several times a day + knees buckle when laughing + vivid images at sleep onset → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.D: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea from left heart failure

whyNot.A: Obstructive apnea does not explain **knees buckling with laughter** or images at sleep onset
whyNot.B: Central apnea does not explain **knees buckling with laughter** or images at sleep onset
whyNot.C: Hypoventilation syndrome occurs with obesity and CO2 retention; her features are **sleep attacks, laughter-triggered collapse and vivid images**
whyNot.D: Nocturnal dyspnea is waking short of breath; she has **sleep attacks by day** with laughter-triggered collapse

why: Daytime sleep attacks, **cataplexy** (loss of tone with laughter) and hypnagogic hallucinations are narcolepsy. It results from loss of orexin (hypocretin) neurons in the lateral hypothalamus, and REM sleep starts within minutes of falling asleep. Modafinil treats the sleepiness.
